biocides-and-chemical-treatment.description: Chemical biocide products, dosing strategies, and treatment programs for industrial water systems. Covers oxidizing biocides (chlorine, bromine, chlorine dioxide, ozone, peracetic acid) and non-oxidizing biocides (isothiazolones, glutaraldehyde, DBNPA, quaternary ammonium compounds). Includes biocide selection, rotation strategies, dose calculations, contact time, pH effects on efficacy, and shock vs continuous dosing.
examples: How Chlorine Effectiveness Drops at High pH
When to Rotate Oxidizing and Non-Oxidizing Biocides
Choosing Between Bromine and Chlorine for Alkaline Cooling Systems
On-Site Chlorine Dioxide Generation for Cooling Towers
DBNPA Dosing Strategy for Cooling Water Microbial Control
notFor: Microbial growth mechanisms and biofilm structure → use biological-control-and-prevention
Legionella-specific treatment regimens → use legionella-specific-control-and-prevention
Long-term biocide program effectiveness across system types → use case-studies-and-transition-planning

biological-control-and-prevention.description: Microbial ecology, biofilm formation, and biological fouling in industrial water systems. Covers microbial growth mechanisms, biofilm matrix structure, ATP monitoring, microbial sampling and testing, regrowth dynamics, and prevention strategies that go beyond chemical dosing. Includes how biofilms resist biocide penetration and why microbial tolerance develops.
examples: How Biofilm Resists Biocide Penetration
Why ATP Monitoring Detects What Plate Counts Miss
Sublethal Biocide Exposure and Microbial Tolerance Development
Identifying Common Cooling Tower Microorganisms
Green Algae and Photosynthetic Growth on Cooling Tower Fill
notFor: Specific biocide products and dosing → use biocides-and-chemical-treatment
Legionella-specific risk assessment and treatment → use legionella-specific-control-and-prevention
Filter and membrane fouling mechanics → use filtration-and-membrane-systems

case-studies-and-transition-planning.description: Real-world customer case studies, before/after comparisons, and planning documents for transitioning from one treatment approach to another. Covers technology migrations (e.g., chlorine to chlorine dioxide, copper-silver to ozone), reclaim water transitions, equipment retrofits, and lessons learned from specific installations. Pairs each case with quantitative outcomes and operational gotchas.
examples: Ashburn VA Reclaim Water Case History in Open and Closed Cooling Systems
Transitioning a Hospital Cooling Plant from Chlorine to Chlorine Dioxide
Switching from Phosphonate to Polymer Inhibitor: A Year-Long Comparison
Data Center Migration from Conductivity-Based to Real-Time Monitoring
Six-Month Results from a Closed-Loop Glycol-to-Inhibited-Water Conversion

General how-to procedures without specific customer context → use system-maintenance-and-operations
Industry trend overviews not tied to a specific installation → use market-and-industry

closed-loop-systems.description: Closed-loop hydronic systems including hot water, chilled water, and glycol loops. Covers makeup water tracking, leak detection, inhibitor selection for closed loops (nitrite, molybdate, sulfite-based), oxygen scavenging, pH and reserve maintenance, and compliance documentation specific to closed loops. Includes why tight loops should show near-zero makeup water usage.
examples: Why Closed-Loop Makeup Meter Logs Matter for Compliance
Choosing Between Nitrite and Molybdate Closed-Loop Inhibitors
Diagnosing High Makeup Water on a Chilled Water Loop
Glycol Concentration and Inhibitor Reserve in Closed Loops
Sulfite Dosing for Oxygen Scavenging in Hot Water Systems

Scale and corrosion mechanisms applicable to all system types → use scale-and-corrosion-inhibition
Direct-to-chip and immersion cooling loops → use direct-to-chip-cooling

company-and-team.description: Content about Nereus the company. Covers company mission and what Nereus does, team bios and leadership, pricing and contact information, product positioning and value proposition, and how Nereus differs from competing platforms or service providers. Marketing-oriented content that introduces or describes the company itself.

Meet the Nereus Team

cooling-tower-operations-and-management.description: Day-to-day operation of open recirculating cooling towers. Covers cycles of concentration, blowdown control, makeup water management, drift and evaporation, fill maintenance, basin cleaning, fan and pump operation, seasonal startup/shutdown, and operator routines. The mechanical and operational side of cooling tower management, as distinct from the chemistry side.
examples: Setting Cycles of Concentration for an Open Recirculating Tower
What Role Does Airflow Play in Open Cooling Tower Performance
Seasonal Startup Checklist for Idle Cooling Towers
Basin Cleaning and Fill Inspection Best Practices
Diagnosing Drift and Evaporation Loss in Cooling Towers

direct-to-chip-cooling.description: Liquid cooling systems for high-density computing including direct-to-chip cooling, rear-door heat exchangers, and immersion cooling. Covers fluid selection (water, dielectric fluids, glycol blends), loop design and topology, leak detection at the chip and rack level, fluid quality monitoring, and the operational differences between data-center liquid cooling and traditional building cooling.
examples: Water Quality Requirements for Direct-to-Chip Cooling Loops
Choosing Between Single-Phase and Two-Phase Immersion Cooling
Leak Detection Strategies for Rack-Level Liquid Cooling

filtration-and-membrane-systems.description: Filtration and membrane technologies for industrial water treatment. Covers side-stream filters, sand filters, cartridge filters, bag filters, reverse osmosis, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, and nanofiltration. Includes filter sizing, backwash cycles, membrane fouling mechanisms, cleaning chemistry (CIP), differential pressure monitoring, and when filtration replaces or complements chemical treatment.
examples: Sizing a Side-Stream Filter for an Open Cooling Tower
How RO Membrane Fouling Differs from Scale Formation
Backwash Cycle Optimization for Sand Filters
Clean-in-Place Chemistry for Spiral-Wound Membranes
When to Choose Bag Filters Over Cartridge Filters

scale-and-corrosion-inhibition.description: Mineral scale formation, corrosion mechanisms, and the inhibitor chemistries that prevent both. Includes saturation indices (LSI, RSI, Puckorius) and how to interpret them.
